$comment: Hand-verified pins for the build-time tools World Downloader Studio bundles
inside its own Windows installer, read by scripts/fetch-dependencies.mjs.
Every 'url' below was downloaded and its bytes hashed independently (sha256sum,
not just trusting a published checksum file) before this file was committed:
- jre:    verified against the official *.zip.sha256.txt published beside it
- gh:     verified against the official gh_<version>_checksums.txt
- git:    git-for-windows publishes no separate checksum artifact for MinGit;
this 'sha256' is the digest of a copy downloaded directly from the
official github.com/git-for-windows/git release over HTTPS, so it
still pins and verifies an exact known-good file even though there
was no third-party checksum to cross-check it against.
Bumping a version means: download the new archive, compute its real SHA-256,
and update BOTH 'sha256' and 'sizeBytes' here together. fetch-dependencies.mjs
refuses to extract anything whose SHA-256 does not match this file -- an
unverified binary never reaches the installer, full stop.

jre.name: Eclipse Temurin 21 JRE (Windows x64)
jre.purpose: Runs the bundled Java engine (world-downloader.jar) so downloading a world never needs a Java install on the user's machine.

git.name: MinGit (portable minimal Git for Windows)
git.purpose: Powers the World Vault feature (per-world local history, push/publish) so a user never needs a separate Git install.

gh.name: GitHub CLI
gh.purpose: Only used by the World Vault's optional 'publish to a new GitHub repository' action.
gh.bundledByDefaultReason: Bundling gh by default would add another ~14 MB (compressed) / ~40 MB (extracted) to EVERY installer for a path most users never touch, on top of the JRE and MinGit already added for the core download and vault-history features every user does touch. It is fetched on demand instead: pass --with-gh to scripts/fetch-dependencies.mjs (or -WithGh to scripts/windows-build.ps1, or /with-gh to build-installer.bat) to include it in a specific build. When it is not bundled, the application falls back to gh on PATH exactly as it does for every other bundled tool, and reports honestly (never a browser link) when neither is present -- see app/src/main/services/bundled.ts.
